children: (BUILT 2026-08-25, commit e3f0817) a — THE VERB: Probe gains `verb` field (default '' for 27 existing probes); bus post() carries verb in envelope + transit table column; BaseDevice.declared_verbs() lets a device declare verb→handler; BaseShim.deliver() resolves verb → device method internally (Law 6), unknown verb → RED (Law 7). Empty verb falls back to receive() for backwards compat. Proof: test_verb.py, 8 teeth, green twice.

(BUILT 2026-08-29) b — THE ANNOUNCE MENU: BaseShim._announce_menu() publishes declared_verbs() onto the device's own announce channel at wiring time (first pulse). COMPILED — add a handler, it appears, no second edit (Law 1). Announce-channel posts are RECORDS, not deliverable: undelivered() filters to personal channel only, post() pokes only for personal. Proof: test_announce_menu.py (4 teeth: menu matches declared_verbs, empty menu published, on announce channel, does not trigger delivery), green twice, sealed netns.

(BUILT 2026-08-29) c — DELIVERY, THE POKE: BusDevice._delivery_hooks registry with wire_delivery()/unwire_delivery(); post() calls the hook after writing the envelope. BaseShim._wire_delivery() registers _receive_poke on first pulse (device_id guaranteed set); _receive_poke calls _check_mail() which processes ALL undelivered mail (current + retry for earlier failures). Per-pulse _check_mail removed from on_pulse — delivery is event-driven. Backlog drain at wiring time catches mail posted before the first pulse. Proof: test_delivery_poke.py (5 teeth) + updated test_delivery.py (7 teeth), all green twice, sealed netns.

(BUILT 2026-08-29) d — ONE EXCHANGE: BusDevice.request() = post() + correlated read via reply_to (one door, not two — falsifier 4). bus.read() gains reply_to filter. In-process model: the poke chain fires synchronously within post(), so the target's reply is in the transit table by the time post() returns. Timeout raises TimeoutError, never returns empty (CP1). Async post() unchanged (fire-and-forget). Proof: test_exchange.py (5 teeth: correlated reply, loud timeout, one door, async unchanged, exact correlation), green twice, sealed netns.

(BUILT 2026-08-29) e — THE EXTERNAL-DEVICE ADAPTER: ExternalParticipant at cairn/tools/base/external.py — a bus participant with an address, a feed, verbs, and no poke path. Posts via same bus.post(), reads own feed at its own arrival moment, announces menu on announce channel. CC's arrival is a session hook; Akien's is via the web server (both filed edges). Proof: test_external_adapter.py (6 teeth: same bus, own feed, no device needed, menu on announce, reads device announce, unread waits), green twice, sealed netns.

(BUILT 2026-08-29) f — THE FIRST REAL RIDER: the loop that was open since 2026-07-18 is closed. shim._fire posts probe envelopes via bus.post() on the personal channel; the delivery poke (child c) fires at post time and delivers to the target's shim. No new code — child c's infrastructure is the rider's path. Proof: test_first_rider.py (4 teeth: probe arrives, body intact, unwired sits, receipt written), green twice, sealed netns.

filed_edges.edge: CHATTER DAMPING — hysteresis or a hold-down window
filed_edges.why_not_built: Crossing-detection (built 2026-07-25, cairn/tools/base/proofs/test_probe_crossing.py) cures the LEVEL flood: a trigger parked true pokes once. It does NOT cure chatter — a value flapping across the line (89.9 / 90.1 / 89.9) produces a genuine crossing each time, so every flap pokes. That is a real and different defect.
filed_edges.why_it_waits: Damping needs a WIDTH — how much hysteresis, how long a hold-down — and no flapping signal has been measured. Picking a number now would be guessing, and a wrong width silently eats real crossings, which is worse than the chatter (Law 3: nothing is known until measured; Law 7: a suppressor that swallows a true poke is the failure mode we least want).
filed_edges.what_would_open_it: One measured flapping predicate in the running system. The system_rackmount CPU threshold is the likeliest first, since it reads a genuinely noisy value.
filed_edges.shape_when_taken: Declared on the Probe (like while_true), remembered on the shim (like _was_true) — the split is already in place, so this is a widening, not a redesign.

filed_edges.edge: BUS RESIDUE — retention on the durable transit table
filed_edges.why_not_built: Distinct from both crossing and chatter, and it drew blood first: an end-to-end proof passed alone and went red IN THE SUITE, counting 2 pokes because the bus is durable through db_domain and a previous run's message was still sitting in the channel.
filed_edges.why_it_waits: Retention policy is already a filed edge on the bus charter (intention+why.json, edge c). This records that it now has a MEASURED consequence rather than being hypothetical.
filed_edges.the_stopgap: Proofs use the bus's own ephemeral-table pattern (nonce table + teardown). That protects the proofs; it does nothing for the live channel, which still accumulates forever.
filed_edges.kin: The proof-over-live-data trap — assert invariants, never a snapshot count. Second occurrence in one day.

filed_edges: [AKIEN] DOES THE VERB VOCABULARY GET RULED, OR GROWN? A device publishes a menu of what it accepts. If verbs are free-form per device, two devices will name the same act differently and every caller learns both — the roster tax the naming principle exists to kill. If there is a closed core vocabulary, it has to be authored now, before the first device publishes one. This is the same shape as a-pane-declares-its-view's closed kind vocabulary, and the two should be answered together or deliberately apart.
